The results of JEE Advanced 2026 have been announced. This year, 56,880 students qualified for JoSAA Counselling, which is 2,502 more than last year.
A total of 179,694 students appeared for the examination, including 139,131 boys and 40,562 girls. Among the qualified candidates, 46,773 are boys and 10,107 are girls.

JoSAA Counselling 2026 Has Started – Plan Your College Choices Carefully

Students can register and fill their college and branch preferences from 2 June to 11 June. With access to 900+ programmes across 138 institutions, it is important to prepare a well-planned preference list based on your rank, interests, and previous years' opening and closing ranks.

featured_reviews.name: The Kalakar Guy
featured_reviews.review_text:
I joined this institute for the NEET batch, expecting good guidance and a disciplined learning environment. Unfortunately, my experience has been quite disappointing.

Faculty and Teaching Quality:
The institute claims that all faculty members are trained from Kota, but that does not seem accurate.

The chemistry teacher often appears unsure while teaching. He frequently refers to the book and struggles with pronunciations and explanations. The pace is extremely slow, and even simple numerical problems take too long. Most classes involve reading from PDF notes displayed on the screen, similar to online one-shot lectures but with less clarity and interaction. He also fails to connect or revise topics properly, which makes it very difficult to understand the subject.

The physics teacher is knowledgeable and teaches at a good level. However, he moves too quickly through the syllabus and completes topics in a rush, leaving little time for proper revision or question practice.

The biology teacher initially seemed approachable and friendly, but over time his attitude became inconsistent. He often goes off-topic and spends a lot of time discussing personal opinions and unrelated issues. He sometimes makes unnecessary remarks about students instead of encouraging them. During doubt sessions, he gives long explanations but often does not answer the actual question directly.

Management and Administration:
The management is disorganized. Classes are frequently shifted without notice, and extra lectures are scheduled at random. Timetable discipline is poor; breaks are often skipped or shortened, and faculty members are sometimes late. It feels like the administration is more focused on fee collection than academic quality or student comfort.

Infrastructure and Facilities:
The infrastructure is below standard. Cleanliness is poor, and drinking water is often unavailable until noon because the supply arrives late. The air cooling system rarely works properly, making classes uncomfortable. There is constant noise from construction work like drilling or hammering during lectures. Garbage bins are usually full, forcing students to keep wrappers and waste in their own bags.

Academic Environment:
The overall classroom environment lacks discipline. Many students are not serious, and the faculty makes little effort to maintain focus or order. Coordination between subjects is weak, and the physics portion usually ends just a day before the test, leaving no time for revision. Chemistry classes, in particular, lack conceptual clarity and proper teaching methods.

Overall Experience:
Except for physics, the teaching quality is poor, management is unorganized, and facilities are not maintained properly. The environment is not suitable for serious NEET aspirants. There is little attention to student comfort, consistency, or conceptual development.

Final Verdict:
I would strongly advise students and parents to personally visit the institute before enrolling. Attend demo classes if possible and carefully observe the teaching quality, infrastructure, and management. In my opinion, there are better coaching options available that offer structured teaching, better facilities, and genuine student support.
